reasons: Deviation classification is correct: 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of bespoke Deliverables in Vendor and gives Customer only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term, which fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense).

Redline is actionable and directionally right: it reverses the assignment to Customer, adds a present assignment of right, title and interest on creation, and expressly preserves Vendor's pre-existing IP and Vendor Technology via the cross-reference to 14.3, so no Customer IP/Data is assigned to Vendor and no joint ownership is created.

The advisory changed-character ratio (0.72) is justified here — reversing the direction of an ownership grant and removing the revocable term-limited licence cannot be done with a smaller edit; the surrounding sections (13.2 licence-back, 14.1/15.1 Customer Data and Customer IP, 14.4 no joint ownership) are correctly left alone.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense) if Vendor must retain title.
